prompt:
You receive 5 images. Image 1 is the LAYOUT SKETCH of the finished 1920x1080 game screen: a crude flat-colour blocking that fixes the exact composition - camera, horizon, wall and floor lines, and the position, size and outline of every object. Repaint image 1 into a finished painting: keep every line and every block exactly where it is and exactly as large as it is, paint each block as the object described below, do not move, enlarge, shrink, add or remove anything, and leave no flat colour areas or hard geometric edges. Images 2-4 are photos of the real place (geography, architecture, materials and real details to paint from; they are references only, do not copy their camera, cars, people, signs or weather). Image 5 is a finished background painting from our game: use it ONLY as the reference for the painting technique (brushwork, palette, edge softness, level of detail, line quality); do not copy anything from its scene.

Place: the inner room (chronochamber) of the fictional temporary Atlas pavilion on the gravel plateau east of the real Rotunda on Chopok (2,004 m), Low Tatras, Slovakia. Image 2 is an approved painting from our game of this very room: light larch wood-panelled walls, a brushed-steel console plate with engraved symbols (circle, cross, square, triangle), an amber emergency lamp above it, a big window with the Rotunda complex outside, a wooden table with a brass desk lamp and a glass of water (ignore the man; keep the room's look). Images 3 and 4 are photos of the real view west from the plateau: the Rotunda (stone base, glass drum, red ring roof) between the long dark station wings on stilts, the grey rocky plateau. Paint this room from a new camera as described below, with the real Rotunda in the window so it is clear where we are.

Brief: the fictional interior of the same exhibition pavilion: four ports and Viktor at a table; through the window the silhouette of the Rotunda shows where we are. Bright midday light from the big window, warm light from the desk lamp, a calm, tense, quiet room. No hidden countdown, no science-fiction look: simple wood, steel and cables.

Camera: standing in the room, about 1.6 m high, looking straight at the back wall, which is parallel to the picture; vertical lines stay vertical; the horizon is at y ~470. Keep this exact geometry from the sketch: the low timber ceiling with beams down to y ~200; the wood-panelled back wall with a darker wainscot (y 560-700) down to the plank floor at y 700; the long steel console plate at x 72-578 (y 370-514) with the four ports in a row; the amber emergency lamp at x 295-353 (y 255-327); the big window at x 700-1520 (y 250-565) with the Rotunda in its middle-right; the wooden table at x 720-1265 with its top's back edge at y 605 and a solid wooden front panel down to y ~790; the restore console at x 1595-1805 (top y 520-600, foot y ~728); the wooden door at the right edge (x 1815-1920, y 380-725); the plank floor from y 700 to the bottom edge.

What the sketch blocks are: the low timber ceiling with beams; the light larch wood-panelled walls and the darker wainscot; the big window to the west with the real Rotunda complex on the plateau under a blue sky (the long dark station wings on stilts, the stone base, the glass drum with its red ring roof, the grey rocky plateau, a few snow patches); the wooden table with a solid front panel, a brass desk lamp and a glass of water on its top; the free-standing restore console; the wooden door; the worn wooden plank floor.

Interactive props - each painted clearly inside its block, the same size as its block, easy to recognise at a glance:
1. the block of the layout sketch at x 92-198, y 388-494 of the 1920x1080 frame (5-10 % from the left, 36-46 % from the top): on the steel console plate, a round metal socket with an engraved circle symbol above it.
2. the block of the layout sketch at x 212-318, y 388-494 of the 1920x1080 frame (11-17 % from the left, 36-46 % from the top): next to it a narrow slot (the size of an audio cassette) with an engraved cross symbol.
3. the block of the layout sketch at x 332-438, y 388-494 of the 1920x1080 frame (17-23 % from the left, 36-46 % from the top): next to it a square socket with an engraved square symbol.
4. the block of the layout sketch at x 452-558, y 388-494 of the 1920x1080 frame (24-29 % from the left, 36-46 % from the top): next to it a socket with an engraved triangle symbol.
5. the block of the layout sketch at x 1595-1805, y 512-677 of the 1920x1080 frame (83-94 % from the left, 47-63 % from the top): the restore console: a steel pedestal with a slanted control top holding four small green input lamps in a row, a key switch and one big round red push button.
6. the block of the layout sketch at x 1092-1172, y 528-610 of the 1920x1080 frame (57-61 % from the left, 49-56 % from the top): a plain glass of water standing on the table, full and untouched.
7. the block of the layout sketch at x 278-370, y 248-340 of the 1920x1080 frame (14-19 % from the left, 23-31 % from the top): an amber emergency lamp in a protective wire cage on a wall bracket above the console plate.
NPC zone at x 905-1065, y 455-607 of the 1920x1080 frame (47-55 % from the left, 42-56 % from the top): an animated character sprite will stand here later, so paint only plain, uncluttered background in it - no person, no figure, no silhouette, no clothes on hooks that read as a person. The character stands behind a table: paint the table's top edge as one straight horizontal line exactly at y 605 across x 875-1095, with its front going down to the floor; above that edge keep only plain background (wall, shelves), no person.
the area of the layout sketch at x 1815-1920, y 380-725 of the 1920x1080 frame (95-100 % from the left, 35-67 % from the top) is the wooden door at the right edge.

Walkable floor: the band at x 0-1920, y 738-1015 of the 1920x1080 frame (0-100 % from the left, 68-94 % from the top) is the worn wooden plank floor - one continuous flat surface with no step, no rug and nothing standing on it: no chairs, no boxes, no cables, no people. Only daylight from the window and soft shadows.

Fiction rules: the ports, the restore console and the pavilion are fictional; no logos, no brand names, no readable text or digits anywhere (only the four engraved symbols). No people (Viktor is a separate sprite), no animals.

The layout sketch is a blocking aid only: paint over all of it. Do NOT draw frames, borders, outlines or boxes around objects, and keep no flat colour block. The finished picture contains no UI, no captions, no text except what is asked for above, no watermark and no people or animals unless stated above.

Style: classic 1990s hand-painted adventure game background. Rich painterly brushwork, slightly exaggerated cartoon proportions with gently curved lines, warm late-afternoon sunlight, saturated but harmonious colours, soft dappled shadows under the trees.
